name: kp-tight-budget
_comment: Same mandate, a $5 monthly ceiling. What is under test is the budget governor's REFUSAL on a night that genuinely tried to spend: seeded with kp-01 only, so the night reaches the governor with exactly one dispatchable idea and the ceiling — not an empty backlog — is what stops it. Evidence the expectation accepts is deliberately narrow (see expectations.mjs): the overnight counts block reporting degraded >= 1, a block whose blockedReason READS as a budget refusal, autopilot dropping below `suggest`, or a metered spend at the ceiling. A night blocked for any other reason — suggest-mode, a rung refusal, no free fleet slot — is NOT a pass here: a dispatch that never reached the governor does not measure it. A night that spends past the ceiling and says nothing is the failure this scenario exists to catch.

dialog.context: We want an owner for the gates, but we are not funding an experiment — five dollars a month, and it must stop when that is gone.
dialog.title: App master for kp on a shoestring

seeds.title: Document KP_TRUSTED_PROXY in .env.example
seeds.description: KP_TRUSTED_PROXY is a real, tested environment variable that the self-hosting production checklist requires operators to set, but it does not appear in .env.example, so a fresh self-host has no way to discover it. Add it, with a comment that says what it does and what happens when it is unset.
